chapter: Other bands, mutes, arrangers and composers
title: Special commissions: a doctor's life story and the Louisiana Purchase flags
summary: DeDroit describes composing music for a patron's life story and a tableau with the French and American flags at a ball.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I'd rather be a side man. Sure. And then you don't have to put up with the captain. And then there's women. And then when I do, I get brainstormed. I had a doctor, he says a letter to my sweetheart. I said that sounds nice. And you know what it was? His whole life. I had to put music to when he was in the army and when he got out of the army, when he recorded his wife, when the first baby was born, all that. He said, you need a score for that. You need an arranger to sit down and time all that stuff. You know? Yeah. And I had a plate, Louisiana, the French flag and the American flag goes up. And I had to compose a piece that contains the Marseilliers and the Stars Spangled Banner. You know? Well I did. But I should have paid for such stuff as that. I don't understand this.
This was during what? How did this work? The Louisiana Purchase.

Yeah. The United States purchased it. So they lowered the French flag or whoever it was, the French flag, and put the American flag on it. What was this so? At a corner of a ball. I see. So I had to play something muted and had the French sport sound sad and the Stars Spangled Banner, you know? It sounds good even if I did do it. I don't think anybody notices but me.
